questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that there was no restriction on which courses I could choose in UUC (University College Cork). It was also crucial to me that they spoke english, and therefore I did not need a proof of language-level prior to my exchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The sites and groups presented at the orientation was useful, and so was the emails I received during my stay. I never had any problem finding information. The UCC site was likewise accessible

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. You have to let go of the idea that housing in Ireland is cheap, but thereafter there are several options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think that I have any comments on this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration to UCC was fairly easy, and straight forward. However, the approvals for courses (these must be approved by the professor teaching the course) came in quite late, and I had to make several changes. This gave som stressfull first weeks, where I had to attend courses where I didn't know whether I was accepted or not, and didn't had acces to the online learning material. It all sorted out in the end, and the international office is very mindful of the problems that it may cause, but I wish that I knew that this was standard practice before I was there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office is open during office hours, and was always helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change more than half of my courses. Not because of my academic level, but because of limited number of students in each course. But the courses that I did end up having was good, and I don't feel like I have missed out on anything

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience!! It will all sort out at the end, but it might not happen as quickly as everyone wants. And also don't spam the international office - they are doing the best they can

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I deliberately chose courses where I had heard about the main topics before. For me, it was a great strategy because I could focus on understanding the knew ways of teaching and understand the irish professors. But because of this I have a feeling of the courses being "easy" and not as challenging as I would have experienced at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very different. I though that differences would be minor, but that was not the case. At UCPH we are used to learning through class discussions and having many online tools available to us. At UCC the focus is quite different - here they have a lot of multiple choice quizzes and the teaching is therefore also with a different focus. It is different but that is also part of the experience

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BC3004 - Cell signalling 
BC6001 - Cell and molecular biology 
MB3007 - Molecular genetics and genomics 
MB3012 - Transmission and epidemiology of infectious diseases 
MB4030 - Advanced medical microbiology and immunology 
NT2013 - Fundamentals of Nutrition (part 1)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked my cell biology course, and would recommend this. The lectures are good and understandable and we had laboratory work as well. 
Also, the course on Molecular genetics and genomics were very interesting and well delivered by the professors on the course 
Cell and molecular biology was a challenge, but we worked a lot in groups and it was a great way to get to know the irish students and their costumes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think that I found any unexpected expenses. Just be mindful that living (housing + food) is not cheaper in Ireland compared to Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think that I expected that food was a bit cheaper than it was. However, snacks and crisps are extremely cheap ;)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As a visiting student at UCC you have access to all clubs (which has teams in all sports ever imagined) and societies (which is non-sport group activities). All these are great and welcoming to visiting students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved traveling across Ireland. It gave such a great look into irish culture and differences.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Dublin, Blarney castle, Cobh, Kinsale, Galway, Cliffs of Moher. Buy a guidebook and cross of all the sights ;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It think it was fairly easy, however it is wrong to enter an exchange semester with the idea that adapting to another culture (no matter the similarity) is no problem at all - it takes some adjustment and reflections within one self

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most of the irish students are quite chatty. A simple "how are you" will bring you a long way

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think there are any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The irish are straight forward. If they finde something unacceptable they will tell you. It is freeing and nice

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) English with the Cork accent is hard to understand (really hard), but you will get there. Don't get discouraged if you understand anything the first weeks 

2) If possible, choose courses where you find the topic easy. You have enough on your plate as a visiting student in a new country, as it is - leave brain space to all other important things 

3) Engage in UCC activities. It is only you that is accountable for entering clubs/societies or other things put on by the collage. Do it!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to understand different teaching methods/focuses, and what that means for my learning. I have loved my time at UCC, but I have also found that the understanding of topics that I get through UCPH is great and top-level

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely understanding Cork-english

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
